Definition: from G3844 and οἴχομαι (to depart); to escape along, i.e. be gone:--past.
BiblicalUsage: Paroichomai means to pass away, to be gone, to escape along. It appears once, in Acts 14:16, where Paul says God in times past suffered all nations to walk in their own ways.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God let the nations walk their own ways for a time, and the patience of that longsuffering is the same patience that now calls them to repent.
